title: What each film holds is known: its picture, its sound and every audio and subtitle track
description: Serves PRODUCT.md: "Any film plays, and plays well ... with the audio and subtitles they chose. No codec, HDR format or subtitle kind is second-class." Playback can't decide how a film plays, and a viewer can't pick a track, until what each file holds has been read. The engine's file reading is carried over here, with the audit's findings on reading film files addressed (D-20261128-audit-findings).
acceptanceCriteria: For each version, the server knows its length, its picture (codec, size, HDR kind) and every audio and subtitle track inside it or kept beside it as a file, each with its language and its marks as the file gives them: default, forced, for the deaf or hard of hearing, audio description, commentary.
It knows what it needs to send the picture as it is where a device plays it, read without reading the whole film.
Reading any one file takes bounded time and memory; a file that can't be read is reported with its reason and never holds up the others.
Reading a film's index from object storage costs a bounded number of requests, whatever the file's structure.
A file is read once per revision: a rescan of an unchanged file reads nothing of it again.
After a file is replaced, a track identity from the old file is refused with a reason; it never names another track.
The design states what reading costs per film, on each kind of storage.
notes: Audit group 4, before the collection's reads are relied on. Chapters may be read here if they come for free with the same read; chapter pictures are stage 5.
